top_story: The UN’s finding that 2025 was the deadliest year on record for aid workers, with Gaza again the most lethal setting, underscores how the war’s baseline conditions have collapsed protections for civilians and those trying to reach them. That pattern sharpened on 18 August near Qabatiya, where Israeli soldiers reportedly detained Palestinian residents and marked numbers on their foreheads before interrogation, reinforcing a climate of humiliation and coercive control in the occupied West Bank as well as Gaza. Hours later, Washington unsealed charges against 17 people tied to an Iran-backed hacking campaign, showing how the regional confrontation is also being fought through cyber operations and legal retaliation far from the battlefield. The combined picture is of a conflict system expanding across physical and digital arenas while steadily eroding humanitarian space and civilian dignity.
